title: Reward ontology v1 conversion policy and source-vocabulary mapping
description: The machine-readable half of reward ontology v1. `policy` is the single source of truth for pipelines/curate_rewards.py: scopes, arithmetic methods, unit-calibration evidence, comparability classes, reason codes, and the ordered classification rules are all read from here. `source_vocabulary` freezes the 2026-08-17 run's 510 reward component keys and 140 structural shapes together with the disposition each key receives and the arithmetic method each shape selects. `expected_classification` freezes the comparability verdict the policy assigns to that run. No source reward is ever discarded: every value is copied verbatim into a reversible sidecar before any annotation is made.
disposition_rules: 4. observed value types subset of {number, value-object} -> magnitude_term
6. observed value types == {object} -> component_container when the key is a declared weighted container, else structural_context
7. observed value types subset of {object, array} -> structural_context

methods.declared_weighted_sum: The reward declares a `weights` object; the total is recomputed as sum_i w_i * c_i, resolving each weight key through `weight_aliases` against the reward itself and every declared weighted container.
methods.declared_weighted_sum_unresolved: A `weights` object is declared but at least one weight key has no resolvable numeric component, so no arithmetic verdict is claimed.
methods.unweighted_component_sum: No `weights` object is declared; the total is recomputed as the plain sum of the numeric sibling components, or of the nested `components` map when the reward carries no numeric siblings.
methods.unweighted_component_sum_unresolved: No numeric component could be resolved, or a nested `components` map coexists with numeric siblings, so no arithmetic verdict is claimed.
methods.no_numeric_total: The reward declares no finite numeric `total`, so there is nothing to reconcile against.
methods.non_object_reward: The reward value is not a JSON object.

ignored_evidence: scopes that name no explicit record id

component_dispositions.declared_total: The reward's own declared `total`. Reconciled against the recomputed total; never summed as a component.
component_dispositions.unit_calibration: Declares units, weights, rounding, or basis. Never summed; read only as conversion evidence.
component_dispositions.narrative_annotation: Free text preserved verbatim in the sidecar. Never summed and never converted.
component_dispositions.component_container: A nested object holding the components a declared weighted or unweighted sum draws from.
component_dispositions.magnitude_term: A numeric (or `{"value": number}`) component that participates in the recomputed total.
component_dispositions.structural_context: A nested object or array that is neither a declared component container nor a numeric term.
component_dispositions.ambiguous_preserve_only: The key is observed with mutually incompatible value types, so no disposition is claimed; it is preserved and never converted.

comparability_classes.magnitude_comparable: Every reward scope in the record carries verified arithmetic and explicit USD-per-unit risk-adjusted calibration, so canonical magnitudes may be emitted and compared across factories.
comparability_classes.sign_order_only: The preference order is verified but at least one side is uncalibrated, so only the sign or the ordering is usable. Canonical magnitudes are refused.
comparability_classes.exclude_from_reward_training: The record carries no usable reward evidence for reward training. Source rewards remain recoverable from the sidecar.

reason_codes.no_source_reward: The record carries no reward scope at all.
reason_codes.ambiguous_preference_reward_scopes: A preference record carries reward scopes beyond the two canonical chosen/rejected pointers.
reason_codes.multiple_reward_scopes: A non-preference record carries more than one reward scope, so no single record-level reward is defined.
reason_codes.noncanonical_reward_scope: The single reward scope is not the canonical `/reward_components` pointer.
reason_codes.reward_arithmetic_mismatch: The declared total disagrees with the recomputed total beyond the declared rounding tolerance.
reason_codes.unsupported_reward_layout: The reward layout admits no arithmetic verdict, so the record is not trusted for reward training.
reason_codes.reward_order_conflicts_with_preference: The chosen side does not score strictly above the rejected side, contradicting the stated preference.
reason_codes.preference_order_verified: Chosen scores strictly above rejected and both sides reconcile arithmetically.
reason_codes.reward_arithmetic_verified: Every retained reward scope reconciles its declared total within tolerance.
reason_codes.explicit_usd_unit_calibration: Every retained reward scope declares a positive USD value per native reward unit.
reason_codes.external_calibration_evidence: The USD-per-unit calibration came from an explicit, per-record external migration sidecar rather than the record's own fields.
reason_codes.magnitude_calibration_missing: No reward scope declares a USD-per-unit calibration, so no canonical magnitude may be claimed.
reason_codes.magnitude_calibration_incomplete: Only some reward scopes declare a usable calibration, so the sides are not magnitude-comparable.
reason_codes.magnitude_calibration_conflict: Structured and textual unit declarations, or record and external evidence, disagree.
reason_codes.magnitude_semantics_missing: A USD-per-unit value is declared without the risk-adjusted semantics the canonical unit requires.

comparability_rules.condition: the record carries no reward scope
reward scopes are not exactly the two canonical preference pointers
either side's declared total disagrees with its recomputed total
either side admits no arithmetic verdict
the chosen total does not exceed the rejected total
both sides reconcile, chosen exceeds rejected, and both sides resolve a positive USD-per-unit calibration
the order is verified but a unit declaration conflicts
the order is verified but only one side resolves a calibration
the order is verified and neither side declares a calibration
more than one reward scope is present
the one reward scope is not the canonical pointer
the declared total disagrees with the recomputed total
the layout admits no arithmetic verdict
a USD-per-unit value is declared without risk-adjusted semantics
the canonical scope reconciles and resolves a positive USD-per-unit risk-adjusted calibration

source_vocabulary.scope_note: The census is taken over `reward_components` scopes so it stays comparable with the training audit's reward vocabulary. The ontology itself also treats a bare `reward` key as a reward scope. Frozen mapping counts are records=195, reward_instances=247, ontology_scope_instances=258. Extra ontology scopes versus the audit's 247 instances are bare `reward` keys (none contribute a canonical magnitude; every one is copied verbatim into its record's reversible sidecar).
source_vocabulary.shape_signature: Sorted `key:subtype` pairs joined by `|`, where subtype is `value-object` for an object carrying a numeric `value`, otherwise the JSON type name. Identical to pipelines/training_audit.py reward_shape.
